title: Alzheimer's Disease_Biological replicate 1
growth_protocol_ch1: Postmortem human hippocampus were cut out from each brain and preserved at −80 °C until RNA preparation. Written informed consent for all subjects was obtained from their families. Neuropathologic changes were examined as described previously (PMID: 20739649).
extract_protocol_ch1: Total RNA was isolated using a combination of Isogen and the RNeasy Mini Kit, according to the manufacturer's instructions.
extract_protocol_ch1.1: The libraries for polyA(+) RNA sequencing were prepared using TruSeq Rapid PE cluster Kit-HS (Illumina; PE-402-4001) and TruSeq Rapid SBS Kit-HS (Illumina; FC-402-4001) according to manufacturer's instructions.
description: Transcriptome expression profiling of postmortem human hippocampus AD brain
data_processing: Sequences were obtained by using HiSeq1500 (Rapid Mode).
data_processing.1: The quality of RNA-Seq reads was checked and preprocessed using fastp (v0.20.1) with --detect_adapter_for_pe option. RNA-Seq reads (FASTQ format) were aligned to RefSeq human reference genome (hg19) using HISAT2 (v2.1.0) software (RRID:SCR_015530). PCR duplicates were removed by Samtools (RRID:SCR_005227). Total paired reads per sample was between 18 million (M) to 59 M reads and mapping efficacy was between 96.62% to 98.65%. For further analysis, StringTie (v2.1.4) was used. Annotation file was created by StringTie and merged with RefSeq Reference Genome Annotation based on human reference genome (hg19). Mapped reads were applied to StringTie (v2.2.1) using the merged annotation file including known transcript annotation and merged transcripts (novel annotations).
data_processing.3: Supplementary_files_format_and_content: The resulting bam files were used to not only calculate gene and transcript expression profile by python script prepDE.py (https://github.com/gpertea/stringtie/blob/master/prepDE.py), but also to obtain TPM (Transcripts Per Kilobase  Million) values. Bioconductor package edgeR (v3.28.1) was used for differential expression analysis and three separate excel files were produced as processed files for all samples.
contact_institute: Medical Institute of Bioregulation, Kyushu University

data_processing: Sequences were obtained by using HiSeq1500 (Rapid Mode).
data_processing.1: The quality of RNA-Seq reads was checked and preprocessed using fastp (v0.20.1) with --detect_adapter_for_pe option. RNA-Seq reads (FASTQ format) were aligned to RefSeq human reference genome (hg19) using HISAT2 (v2.1.0) software (RRID:SCR_015530). PCR duplicates were removed by Samtools (RRID:SCR_005227). Total paired reads per sample was between 18 million (M) to 59 M reads and mapping efficacy was between 96.62% to 98.65%. For further analysis, StringTie (v2.1.4) was used. Annotation file was created by StringTie and merged with RefSeq Reference Genome Annotation based on human reference genome (hg19). Mapped reads were applied to StringTie (v2.2.1) using the merged annotation file including known transcript annotation and merged transcripts (novel annotations).
data_processing.3: Supplementary_files_format_and_content: The resulting bam files were used to not only calculate gene and transcript expression profile by python script prepDE.py (https://github.com/gpertea/stringtie/blob/master/prepDE.py), but also to obtain TPM (Transcripts Per Kilobase  Million) values. Bioconductor package edgeR (v3.28.1) was used for differential expression analysis and three separate excel files were produced as processed files for all samples.
